title: spcz: a Rust CLI for macOS displays, desktops and windows, with arngz rebuilt on it
objective:
Build spcz, a Rust CLI in Utilz that reads and changes macOS displays, desktops and windows, with commands and JSON output. Then rebuild arngz on spcz, so that arngz does not use Hammerspoon.

- spcz supports macOS 27 and later only (hv decision 48).
- spcz needs no SIP change. It injects no code into the Dock or WindowManager, and it uses exported names only (hv decision 47).
- Compatibility with Hammerspoon, its Lua API or its config file is not a goal (hv decision 46).
- arngz keeps its desks. A run does not lose a window that it has named, and each desk entry keeps the windows it was recorded with (STca1b7f9's open parts, hv decision 66).

hv decisions 43, 46, 47, 48, 66 and 69, 26 and 27 Nov 2026.
context:
hv proposed spcz on 26 Nov 2026 (hv decision 43), after cc found that every hs.spaces call that needs Mission Control fails on macOS 27.2.1. hv's words: "there are two orthogonal concerns here: 1. Manipulate the macOS spaces, desktops, and windows programmatically [spcz, as a working title] 2. Manage a set of desktop/space/app arrangements [arngz]". 2.15.0 shipped arngz's own Mission Control finder, mc.lua, as a stopgap (hv decision 44). The spcz thread opens after the 2.15.0 cut, design first (hv decisions 43 and 66).

The design starts from vc's draft v0.1 (~/Devel/scratch/utilz-vc/spcz/design-draft.md, 26 Nov 2026), with hv's rulings on it:

- spcz is a plain Rust CLI with commands and JSON output. Its design reads Hammerspoon's and yabai's source as a reference and cites it (hv decision 46).
- spcz has nothing to do with yabai's approach, and it never needs a SIP change. yabai's notes stay in the design as a reference only (hv decisions 47 and 48).
- spcz supports macOS 27 and later only (hv decision 48).
- For a window move, the spike tries Hammerspoon's method first, ported from its MIT source with a citation. The title-bar hold is the fallback. The spike's result on macOS 27 decides (hv decision 48).

Carried in from STca1b7f9 (hv decision 66): its open criteria AC-026eadfc.1 to .4 (the window registry), AC-b9d4e976.1 to .8 (an entry keeps the windows it was recorded with), AC-dca427e7.5 (the route through another display, in a live run), AC-ad94d40b.4 to .6 (the Mission Control leg) and AC-322a6511.6 and .8 (the hold's log, and the help for a failed window filter and a failed create). STca1b7f9 is cancelled as superseded when spcz's criteria exist.

Carried in from issue I7fce35c (hv decision 69): its part (6), windows lost mid-run, and the remaining piece of its part (1), the windows that a failed window filter cannot name. Both ride the window registry. I7fce35c closes with a resolution that names where each of its parts went.

design.md says how spcz meets each carried criterion, or why it drops one. hv reviews the design before any code.
